Test instance (25x16): background 5. Same-color 2 bars on top row cols 3-8 and bottom row cols 10-15. Color-6 singleton markers at zero-based (6,7),(15,8), and adjacent pair (21,5),(21,6). A common tempting hypothesis is to shift marker columns by the offset between bar starts (+7), turn markers to 4, and draw vertical lines. We tried eight variants, all WRONG: (1) shifted columns, each topward to its own marker row; (2) shifted columns, nearest top/bottom direction; (3) direct columns, nearest direction; (4) full-height shifted columns; (5) shifted columns topward to max marker row; (6) shifted columns downward from markers; (7) both direct and shifted topward lines; (8) direct columns all topward. Therefore none of these full-grid hypotheses is correct; don't reuse them without fresh reasoning. Output dimensions were same in demos, but this task instance's correct output is unknown.

All eight demo observations, using zero-based coordinates:
1. 24x17, bg2; color8 bars top row c0-6 and bottom row c7-13; zero markers at (10,12),(15,10),(20,13). Output preserves bars, converts each marker to 4, draws zero vertical fills at c3,c5,c6 through nearly the full interior, and also extends source columns c12 from r11 down, c10 from r16 down, c13 from r21 down. Suggests translated correspondence, but output for zero marker is unusual.
2. 6x29, bg3; color1 bars top row c16-24 and bottom row c0-8; color7 markers at (2,20),(2,21),(2,24),(3,19). Output turns markers to4 and fills color7 at mapped columns c4,c5,c8,c3 from top row through row3 (all projected columns reach deepest marker row). This confirms a start-relative horizontal shift -16 for this example, but does NOT establish the test's correct fill direction/extent for its different geometry.
3. 24x29, bg0; color7 vertical rails at left c0,r7-11 and right c28,r19-23; color6 markers (7,14),(9,21),(10,22),(11,10). Output converts markers to4 and fills horizontal color6 from left rail to each marker on its row; separately, rows19,21-23 are filled across much of the width from the right rail.
4. 22x29, bg5; color6 bars top row c5-13 and bottom row c20-28; zero markers (8,8),(14,13),(17,10). Output markers become4; mapped zero columns c23,c28,c25 fill most/all vertical interior, and original columns are extended down from their markers. Again zero markers exhibit a different-looking two-sided effect.
5. 14x6, bg0; color8 vertical rails right c5,r8-10 and left c0,r11-13; color3 markers (9,3),(10,1). Output markers become4; color3 fills horizontally from each marker toward the right rail. Rows12-13 also gain color3 across c1-5.
6. 30x8, bg8; color3 rails right c7,r0-10 and left c0,r11-21; color5 markers in the central area. Output changes marker cells to4 and draws color5 horizontally from the left rail to each marker for rows aligned with that rail.
7. 16x25, bg3; color0 bars top row c0-8 and bottom row c10-18; color2 markers at (4,12),(4,17),(5,13),(7,10),(7,15),(9,14),(10,11),(12,18). Output changes marks to4 and draws broad/intersecting color2 lines/areas tied to the bars. Some projected columns and source-side fill are visible; this is another useful but complex case.
8. 8x5, bg8; color0 bars top row c2-3 and bottom row c0-1; single color6 marker (6,3). Output changes marker to4, fills c1 with color6 from r0 through r6, and also fills source column c3 on r1-5. Bars unchanged.

General safely supported facts across examples: outputs keep original dimensions; edge bars usually remain unchanged; isolated interior marker cells often become color4; fill color is often the marker color; fills align perpendicular to edge bars. But exact correspondence, whether same-column and shifted copies are both filled, which side to extend toward, and effects of marker color 0 remain unresolved. The top/bottom-bar demos suggest offset mapping in some cases, but the failed test shows that simple start-offset rays are insufficient. Consider collecting/plotting all demo arrays and infer a rule before submitting; avoid overconfidently applying only the apparent +7 shift.'''
